_comment: When are two spellings of a symbol the same instrument?
This question is answered in two languages, and it has to be
answered identically in both. The engine decides whose candles and
whose contract specification are whose; the desk decides which
spec to price a ticket with, in the browser, because a round trip
per mouse move while dragging a stop is not something anyone would
ship. A future native front end will be the third.
Three implementations of one rule is three chances to disagree, so
the cases live here, once, and every implementation is tested
against this file. Adding a case here is how the rule changes.
The rule itself: fold away a broker's account-type suffix when it
is its own separator-delimited token of up to four letters -
XAUUSD.m, XAUUSD-ECN, XAUUSD_i are all XAUUSD. Fold away nothing
else. A glued suffix is not folded, because nothing distinguishes
the 'm' of XAUUSDm from the 'T' of EURUSDT. A remainder containing
a digit is not folded either, because that names a contract rather
than an account type: CL.F25 and CL.G25 are two different futures.
